description: Admin API, proxy listener, main entry point, demo backend, and benchmark client. Depends on FEAT-001 (all foundation modules must exist). This FEAT wires everything into a running process: admin_api/handler.c + json_builder.c, proxy/proxy.c, src/main.c, demo_backend/demo_backend.c, benchmark/benchmark.c, and the admin unit test. After this FEAT the full edgemesh binary, demo_backend, and benchmark_client all build and run.
steps: Create src/admin_api/json_builder.c: json_escape_string(const char *in, char *out, size_t out_size) — iterates input bytes, escapes '"' as '\"', '\\' as '\\\\', '\r' as '\\r', '\n' as '\\n', '\t' as '\\t', and control chars (< 0x20) as '\\uXXXX', writes result into out bounded by out_size, always NUL-terminates. json_build_*() helpers: json_build_health(), json_build_overview(), json_build_backends(), json_build_metrics(window_seconds), json_build_benchmark_latest() — each allocates a fixed 64KiB stack buffer (or heap if needed), fills it via snprintf-chained writes, and returns it as a heap-allocated string the caller must free. All dynamic values (strings, timestamps) go through json_escape_string before insertion.

Create src/admin_api/handler.c: handle_admin_request(int client_fd). Reads request headers from client_fd (bounded 16KiB, timeout 5s using read_with_timeout). Parses method and path. Dispatches: GET /api/v1/health -> json_build_health(); GET /api/v1/overview -> json_build_overview(); GET /api/v1/backends -> json_build_backends(); PUT /api/v1/policy -> read body (bounded 4KiB, reject 413 if larger), parse JSON field 'policy', validate value is 'round_robin' or 'least_connections', acquire policy_mutex, update g_pool.policy, release mutex, return 200 JSON; GET /api/v1/metrics?window_seconds=N -> parse query param (validate 10-300 range, default 60), call json_build_metrics(); GET /api/v1/benchmarks/latest -> json_build_benchmark_latest() which opens results/latest.json read-only (fixed path only, no caller input), parses it, returns content or {available:false}. Unknown path: 404. Wrong method: 405. For every response add CORS headers (check Origin header against whitelist: http://localhost:5173 and http://127.0.0.1:5173 only — if match, echo that exact origin back; never use '*'). Handle OPTIONS preflight: respond 200 with Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, PUT, OPTIONS and Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type.

Create src/proxy/proxy.c: proxy_start(backend_pool_t *pool, metrics_t *metrics) creates a listening TCP socket bound to 127.0.0.1:8080 with SO_REUSEADDR. Maintains a semaphore or counter capping concurrent workers at MAX_CONNECTIONS=64. accept() loop: on new connection spawns a pthread (detached) passing a proxy_worker_args_t struct {client_fd, pool, metrics}. proxy_worker_thread: (1) read_with_timeout for headers up to 16KiB; (2) parse_request(); (3) on parse error send_error_response and goto cleanup; (4) select_backend() — on -1 send 503 and goto cleanup; (5) connect to backend with timeout (use non-blocking connect + select); (6) build forwarded GET request (path+query from parsed request, add Host: <backend_addr>, Connection: close, X-Forwarded-For: <client_ip>, skip hop-by-hop headers); (7) send to backend with write_all using MSG_NOSIGNAL; (8) read backend response headers (bounded); (9) forward full response to client using write_all with MSG_NOSIGNAL; (10) record metrics; cleanup: close client_fd, close backend_fd, release_backend() ALWAYS called if selection succeeded. Use goto cleanup throughout to guarantee release_backend is called on every exit path. proxy_stop() sets stop flag and closes listener fd.

Create src/main.c: entry point. sigaction(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN) first. Initialize g_pool via pool_init(). Initialize g_metrics via metrics_init(). Start health worker: health_worker_start(&g_pool). Start metrics tick thread (1-second loop calling metrics_tick()). Start admin listener: admin_listener_start() — separate pthread accepting on 127.0.0.1:9090, for each connection spawns handle_admin_request in a detached thread. Start proxy: proxy_start(&g_pool, &g_metrics). Install SIGINT/SIGTERM handler that sets a global volatile sig_atomic_t g_shutdown=1. Main thread waits (sigsuspend or sleep loop checking g_shutdown). On shutdown: proxy_stop(), health_worker_stop(), join metrics tick thread, close admin listener. Exit 0.

Create src/demo_backend/demo_backend.c: minimal HTTP/1.0 server. argv[1] = port number (validated 1-65535). Creates TCP socket, binds to 127.0.0.1:<port>, listens, accept loop. For each connection: read request (discard), send: 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/plain
Connection: close
Content-Length: N

Backend at port <port>
'. Close connection. No threading needed — sequential is fine for demo. Validate port arg, print startup message 'demo_backend listening on 127.0.0.1:<port>
'.

Create benchmark/benchmark.c: CLI load generator. Parses args: -n <requests> (default 1000, max 100000), -c <concurrency> (default 10, max 256), -t <url> (required, must match http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<path> pattern — reject non-loopback URLs). Spawns <concurrency> pthreads, each sends HTTP GET requests sequentially until total reaches <n>. Uses an atomic counter for work distribution. Records per-request latency (monotonic_ms). After all threads finish: computes duration, rps, bytes/s, p50/p95/p99. Writes results/latest.json and results/latest.csv with all fields from api-contract.md section 8. Includes run_id (bench-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS), completed_at (RFC3339), policy (read from GET /api/v1/health or default 'unknown'), all measured values. Never fabricates numbers — if a measurement is unavailable it is null in JSON.

Create tests/test_admin.c: CTest executable testing admin JSON output and input validation WITHOUT starting a network listener. Tests: json_escape_string with embedded quotes, backslashes, newlines, and null bytes; policy update path — directly call the policy-update logic with valid/invalid JSON strings and verify correct return codes and that invalid input does not mutate g_pool.policy; verify json_build_health() returns valid JSON containing 'status' and 'ok'; verify json_build_backends() returns JSON array with 3 entries (after initializing g_pool); verify oversized body (>4096 bytes) is rejected with correct error code.
acceptance_criteria: cmake --build build --parallel completes for all four targets: edgemesh, demo_backend, benchmark_client, and all test executables
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure: test_admin passes all cases
wsl -e bash -c demo_backend 9001 starts and responds to curl http://127.0.0.1:9001/ with 'Backend at port 9001'
edgemesh binary exists and --help or invocation without args exits cleanly (not segfault)
benchmark_client -n 10 -c 2 -t http://127.0.0.1:8080/ runs (proxy must be running) and writes results/latest.json
No -Werror violations in any compiled translation unit
